findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: Portioned salsa containers are being stored in a cooler where the shelves are coated with mold. The containers are uncovered and are in direct contact with mold spores possibly contaminating food items. Discussed the high risk of cross contamination with the person in charge. Ensure that salsas are moved to a different cooler and the shelves are cleaned to remove the mold. Will follow-up on July 16, 2026.
findings.citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: There were uncovered sauces stored inside of the produce cooler that were directly underneath the air compressor. The ceiling of the cooler also contained a bit of mold accumulation. Ensure that foods are always covered and protected against any possible contamination. Will follow-up on July 16, 2026 to see that foods are covered or discarded.
findings.citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Multiple gnats were observed inside mesh bags that store various produce. The bag of potatoes contained rotten items and the bag was discarded by the PIC. As for the other products, they were transferred to a different container/box as a way to reduce attraction and remove insects. Discussed washing produce thoroughly before prepping for service. Ensure to maintain the premise free of insects and reduce harboring conditions.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The sanitizer solution along the cookline was observed with a concentration well past 200ppm CL. The test strip was shown to the PIC and more water was added to the solution to correct the violation. Ensure that sani solutions are maintained at the concentration recommended by the manufacturer to be sure that food contact surfaces are getting sanitized effectively.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The soda nozzle of the gun holder in the bar area is accumulated with black debris on the inner surfaces. Shown to the PIC. Because this surface is in direct contact with liquids, see that the surface is sanitized every night when closing. Will follow-up on July 16, 2026.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: There were various Time/Temperature control foods that lacked date marking inside of both walk in coolers. These items included meats, sauces, rice, etc. Discussed with the PIC that any TCS foods that are prepared in house must be date marked with the date of preparation. Ensure that TCS foods are never held longer than seven days after they are prepared. Will follow-up on July 16, 2026.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: There was an abundance of gnats mainly in the back storage area where dry goods are stored, as well as the room furthest to the back of the premise (where ice machine is located). The gnats appeared inside of mesh bags that contained whole onions, chile, and potatoes. The facility was instructed to stored onions in a different container/box to remove the trapped insects. While the onions were transferred to a different container, the amount of gnats present will cause for a follow-up. Ensure that the premise is free of insects and be sure to transferred vegetables to sealed tight containers if attracting insects. Will follow-up July 16, 2026.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: The shelves inside of the storage cooler that stores portioned salsas are coated with mold. In addition, the shelves of the walk in cooler contained dried debris. Shown to the PIC and he mentioned having the shelves cleaned as soon as possible. Ensure that shelves are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent mold buildup (and other debris) and to protect against cross contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
The ceiling of both walk in coolers were observed with accumulated mold. Shown to the PIC and he mentioned having the ceilings cleaned soon. Most foods were observed covered, however, there were a few items that lacked covering and were also shown to the PIC. Lids were placed on the uncovered items. Ensure that the cooler ceilings are cleaned as frequently as possible to prevent mold accumulation.

4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.
There was a significant amount of ice build up on the floor, shelves, and packaging of food of the walk in cooler. Shown to the manager and he mentioned that the cooler is suppose to be serviced soon to fix the buildup issue and service the unleveled floor. Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces of equipment are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent buildup.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: There was a significant amount of ice build up on the floor, shelves, and packaging of food of the walk in freezer. Shown to the manager and he mentioned that the freezer will be serviced to reduce ice build up. Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces of equipment are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent buildup.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: The siding of the walk in freezer’s door contains a buildup of mold. The gasket of the freezer door is also in disrepair and could be the reason for ice accumulation. Shown to the PIC. See that the mold is cleaned and that the door is repaired to reduce the amount of ice accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
findings.comment: There is roughly about an inch of sewage starting to back up at the clean out located in front of the triple sink. The PIC mentioned that water backs up when the employees are doing dishes. See that the plumbing is serviced by a license plumber. Ensure that sewage is maintained in a sanitary manner and never present inside of the facility. Will follow-up on July 16, 2026 to see that plumbing is repaired.
findings.citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

findings.title: Garbage and refuse are properly disposed; facilities are maintained.
findings.comment: There was leftover food and beer bottles that appeared left from previous nights inside of the back storage room. There were several gnats swarming the leftover food. Shown to the PIC and the objects were discarded to correct the violation. Discussed that all trash should be removed from the premise when closing for the night to prevent harboring conditions for insects and pest. Ensure to educate staff on the removal of all trash within the facility.
findings.citation_text: 5-502.11 Frequency. REFUSE, recyclables, and returnables shall be removed from the PREMISES at a frequency that will minimize the development of objectionable odors and other conditions that attract or harbor insects and rodents.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: There wasn't any soap available at the hand-sink in the employee bathroom. Discussed with the manager and hand soap was provided to the sink to correct the violation. Ensure that every handwashing sink is supplied with warm running water, hand soap, and paper towels to be sure that hands are getting washed properly.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: There were at least three time/temperature control (TCS) foods that were probed at less than 120F (95F - 120F). The foods were recently placed on the steam table. The kitchen cook was instructed to increase the temperature of  the steam table to be sure that foods are holding at a minimum of 135F internal temperature. Shortly afterwards, the foods were rechecked and temperatures were observed compliant. Violation corrected onsite. Ensure that TCS foods are maintained at the proper hot holding temperature.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: There is an insect glue trap placed directly above the dish table across from the dish machine. Discussed  with the manager that insect traps shall never be stored above food, food prep area, or above areas where clean dishes are handled and stored. Ensure that insect glue traps are never placed in the above mentioned areas to prevent cross contamination of food items.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.13 Insect Control Devices, Design and Installation. (A) Insect control devices that are used to electrocute or stun flying insects shall be designed to retain the insect within the device. (B) Insect control devices shall be installed so that: (1) The devices are not located over a FOOD preparation area; and (2) Dead insects and insect fragments are prevented from being impelled onto or falling on exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: There is a significant gap at the bottom of the back door of the establishment. The gap is at least an inch in size. PIC mentioned that the facility will be having the door replaced very soon. Ensure that all outer doors are closed fitting to prevent the entry of unwanted pests and insects.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces of equipment are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent buildup.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: At the start of the inspection, a drink pitcher was observed inside of the bar’s hand-sink. Discussed with the PIC and the pitcher was removed. Ensure that hand-sinks are never obstructed and are available at all times for employees to wash hands.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The baffles of the ice machine in the back storage room were observed with a significant amount of black mold and other debris. Discussed and shown to PIC. PIC mentioned that a service technician will be contacted to service the machine. Discussed cleaning the baffles in house in between professional services or having the technician company service the machine more frequently. Ensure that food contact surfaces are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent mold build up and possible contamination of food items.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: There are several pieces of unused equipment stored in the back storage room. The PIC is in the process of having the unused equipment removed from the premises. Discussed with PIC that unnecessary pieces of equipment can be seen as litter and act as a harboring environment for unwanted insects and pests. Continue to make progress regarding cleaning and the removal of pieces that are no longer necessary for operation.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.114 Maintaining Premises, Unnecessary Items and Litter. The PREMISES shall be free of: (A) Items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment such as EQUIPMENT that is nonfunctional or no longer used; and (B) Litter.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
findings.comment: The assigned managers are not performing duties as necessary. Employees are not properly trained on handwashing, including when and how to wash hands, creating and testing sanitizer buckets, and properly storing food to prevent cross contamination. There are only 2 Certified Food Protection Managers. None of the other employee have food handler certificates. The inspector will provide educational handouts and arrange a visit with the facility to help get more individuals certified to allow a better understanding of food safety.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.11(A) Demonstration. Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, during inspections and upon request the PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the HAZARD Analysis and CRITICAL CONTROL POINT principles, and the requirements of this Code. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate this knowledge by: (A) Complying with this Code by having no violations of PRIORITY ITEMS during the current inspection.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: There wasn't any hand soap available at the bar hand-sink. Discussed with PIC. Dish soap will be used until hand soap can be provided. Ensure that hand soap is always available at every handsink to be sure that hands are getting washed properly.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: There wasn't any paper towels available at the kitchen handsink. Paper towels were provided to correct the violation. Ensure that paper towels are always available to be sure that hands are getting washed properly.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Overall, the facility struggles with storage order. Raw animal protein was observed being stored over ready-to-eat food items in several coolers throughout the facility. Raw animal protein with higher cooking temperatures were also being stored above proteins with lower cooking temperatures. The inspector will bring proper storage order handouts later in the week to help guide employees with properly storing food. Ensure that raw animal protein is always stored below RTE food and also be sure to store animal protein with a higher cooking temperature below items with lesser cooking temperatures.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The sanitizer bucket in the kitchen area tested at 0ppm (CL). Discussed with PIC and sani bucket was remade and tested again at 100ppm. Ensure that sani buckets are maintained at the proper concentration in order to correctly sanitize food contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The baffles of the ice machine in the back storage room were observed with a significant amount of black mold and pink slime. Discussed and shown to PIC. PIC mentioned that a service technician will be contacted to service the machine. Ensure that food contact surfaces are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent mold build up and possible contamination of food items.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: A sliced tomato stored on the cold table was probed at 64F. PIC mentioned that the tomato was recently sliced and placed on the cold table. The facility was instructed to transfer the tomato to the standing cooler. The violation was corrected on site. Be sure that TCS foods are cold held at 41F or less to ensure proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: A container of cut beef was observed thawing inside of the wash sink. Discussed with PIC that thawing should occur under running water and shall be completely submerged. A flow of running water was provided to correct the violation. Ensure that the facility is always using at least one of the approved thawing methods : submersion under running water, under refrigeration, or through the cooking process.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13(B) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F).

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: There was a significant gap at the bottom of the back door of the establishment. PIC mentioned that the facility will be having doors replaced very soon. Ensure that all outer doors are closed fitting to prevent the entry of unwanted pests and insects.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Overall, several food items were stored uncovered or on the floor of the dry storage closet. These items include, but are not limited to, white rice, dry mixes, and dried peppers. Discussed proper storage of food items with PIC. Ensure that dry foods are always covered and stored at least six inches above the floor to prevent contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: At least 3 large stock pots were observed stored on the kitchen floor. Discussed proper storage of clean equipment with PIC. Ensure that cooking equipment is always stored in a manner that protects against contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: The wash, rinse, and sanitize solutions were in the incorrect order at the bar’s triple sink. The solutions were as followed: wash, sanitize, rinse. Discussed with PIC and solutions were correctly arranged. Ensure that wash sink solutions contain wash solution first, then rinse, and then sanitize.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.18 Warewashing Equipment, Clean Solutions. The wash, rinse, and SANITIZE solutions shall be maintained clean.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: The baffles of the hood system were extremely accumulated with grease. There were droplets starting to form. The facility mentioned that the baffles are cleaned every 1-2 weeks by the employees. The facility was instructed to routinely clean the baffles at least once a week to avoid the grease buildup and possible contamination of food.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment:
There are several leaks at the triple sink in the back of the house. The areas are as followed:
- at both faucets of the triple sink
- underneath the far left basin of the triple sink

Ensure that the triple sink is maintained in good repair and is in leak free condition.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: A cellphone was observed to be placed on a shelf that stores clean dishes in the dish room. Ensure that cellphones are placed in a designated area and not in dish room where clean dishes are stored to protect against contamination.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.110 Using Dressing Rooms and Lockers. (A) Dressing rooms shall be used by EMPLOYEES if the EMPLOYEES regularly change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Facility could not provide proof of food handler certifications for employees. Ensure that employees who are not manager certified obtain a food handler certification if handling food and clean dishes.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.citation_text: 6-501.110 Using Dressing Rooms and Lockers. (A) Dressing rooms shall be used by EMPLOYEES if the EMPLOYEES regularly change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: Observed clean utensils to be stored with food contact surface faced upward along the cookline. Discussed with PIC proper storage technique. Ensure that clean utensils are stored with the handles facing upward to protect against contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-904.11(B) Kitchenware and Tableware. (B) Knives, forks, and spoons that are not prewrapped shall be presented so that only the handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and by CONSUMERS if CONSUMER self service is provided.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: The back outside door was observed propped open. Discussed with PIC and door was shut. Ensure that doors are never propped open top avoid the entry of unwanted insects and pests.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: Chicken in a sink was observed to be thawing improperly. There wasn’t a constant flow of running water. Discussed with PIC and running water was provided. If using the running water thawing method, be sure to always have a constant flow of running water at all times.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13(B) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F).

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment:
Shredded mozzarella and mushrooms were observed to be improperly stored on ice. The ice method is being used to cold hold these food items. The containers of food were pushed further down into the ice so that the bottom and sides are
covered with ice. Be sure that containers are completely covered with ice to ensure that foods are at the proper cold holding temperature.
findings.citation_text: 301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: A container of uncovered tortilla shells was observed to be directly underneath a missing ceiling tile in the dry storage room. Discussed with PIC and shells were moved to a different area. Ensure that food is stored in a manner that protects against contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.
